verdict.rationale: Notion's own docs describe it as a shared system of record. Its official MCP server lets several agent clients (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) read, create and update the same workspace content, and its Agent API exposes session event history, so context can persist in Notion between tools. However, no explicit handoff mechanism or guarantee of context preservation between agents is documented. Missing for 10: a documented agent-to-agent handoff workflow, any evidence that context or state transfers without loss, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can hand off work between tools or agents without losing context or information

citations.quote: Notion MCP lets an MCP client, such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex, connect to your Notion workspace through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Read, create, and update Notion content.

Bring everything into one system of record.
